title: fix: don't announce merged PRs as live before the production release
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
The PR gist and realtime Discord post run when a PR merges to \`main\`, but users only get the change after the next \`production\` deploy. The posts still said things were already live. For example, #15842 was announced as \"Enter's rail now shows the thicker mark\" while production still showed the old mark.

- Adds a deploy status line to the gist prompt input and the Realtime Discord prompt: merged to main, not live yet
- Prompts describe what the change does without claiming it's live (\"now shows\", \"is live\", \"you can now\") and without repeating release timing in every post
- Example blurb and impact guidance updated to match
- Only the prompts change; there's no post-processing

Dry run against #15842 and #15512 gives neutral changelog-style text, e.g. \"Enter's rail gets the thicker lotus lockup\".

gist.headline: The changelog learns patience
gist.blurb: The announcement prompts learn the difference between a merge and a deploy. English has enough tenses to handle this.
gist.summary: The gist and realtime Discord prompts receive merged-to-main, not-yet-production status so they describe PR changes without claiming those changes are live; no post-processing is added.
gist.impact: Generated copy uses phrasing like “Enter’s rail gets the thicker lotus lockup” instead of “now shows” when production still has the previous version.
gist.visual_concept: Show the social pipeline distinguishing a merged PR from a production deploy: Polli edits a small announcement at a cozy desk, while a CRT robot holds two clearly separate status cards beside a code-plant.
gist.image_prompt: In a cozy pixel art garden shed, Polli edits an announcement at a retro desk while a friendly CRT monitor robot holds separate pixel-font cards reading “MERGED” and “PRODUCTION”; a small code-plant grows beside them against a prominent lime green (#ecf874) and warm cream backdrop. The main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings; she wears tiny editor glasses, stays small-to-medium in the scene, and is strictly pixel art, never realistic. Cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes.
